# AI Engineering Compiler v0.3.1

Almost every change in this release comes from one repository adopting 0.2.0
and keeping a log of what it had to wire by hand because the compiler could not
express it. That log is the best kind of bug report, and this is it applied.

These changes were tagged as 0.3.0 but never reached npm, so 0.3.1 is the first
release to carry them. It also hardens the commit guard they introduced.

## Hooks got the vocabulary they were missing

- **Blueprints can declare hooks.** Choosing a workflow used to forfeit the
  entire hook vocabulary, silently — `hooks:` now works in
  `.ai/blueprint.yaml` exactly as it does in a manifest.
- **`turn-end`** compiles to Claude Code's `Stop`, so end-of-turn verification
  gates are expressible.
- **`pre-tool` / `post-tool` with `tools`** let a hook fire for the tools it
  cares about: `tools: [Bash]` for a commit guard. `pre-edit` and `post-edit`
  stay as sugar for the edit tools.
- **Packs can ship hooks**, materialized to `.ai/generated/hooks/` and made
  executable on the way out.

## Adopting a workflow is no longer all or nothing

```yaml
workflow:
  development: spec-driven
  disable: [hook.spec-trailer]
```

Naming something the pack does not contribute fails with a list of what it
does, so a typo cannot quietly do nothing.

## spec-driven ships its mechanism, not just its opinion

The pack's rules said "write the spec first, then implement" and left you to
enforce it. It now ships the `Spec:` commit trailer convention, a rule
documenting it along with the CI check, and a hook that refuses a commit
without one.

The hook reads the command the way a shell does: it finds git after global
options (`git -C dir commit`), inside `$(...)`, and behind `env`, `xargs`,
`sh -c`, or `eval`. It reads the message from `-m`, `-F`, or a here-document,
and asks `git interpret-trailers` whether a `Spec:` trailer is there. A
`Spec:` in the subject line or a shell comment does not count, and neither
does `--amend` written inside a message. A message it cannot read without
running something is refused, with instructions to write it literally. The
hook still fails open when it breaks: no node, no git, or a malformed payload
lets the commit through. An adversarial test table covers each case.

The rule's CI snippet now checks every commit in a pull request for a real git
trailer. The hook can be talked around (a git alias, a script that commits);
CI is the check that holds.

## Upgrading

Blueprint users: run `aie sync` — the pack is now version 2, so `aie check`
will report drift until you do.

**One behavior change worth reading.** Because the pack now contributes a hook,
it begins merging into `.claude/settings.json` for the first time. Everything
you wrote there by hand is preserved — that guarantee has not changed — but the
file is now touched where previously it was not. If you would rather keep it
entirely yours, add `disable: [hook.spec-trailer]` to your blueprint.

## Also

`uses: akin-oz/ai-engineering@v0` now resolves. Only exact version tags existed
before, while the README documented a floating major tag that did not — the
`v0` tag now exists and moves with each release.

The deprecated `ai` binary now names 0.4.0 as its removal release, rather than
removing it in the same release that unblocks an adopter.
